answer: Attention latency ladder.** Each new identity must complete a slow serial task—a fixed sonnet transcription verified by cross-model agreement—before it can act or be paid. The task scales in duration per account per day, so an attacker's parallel fleet pays in wall-clock time, not just compute. An onyx-tier queue limits simultaneous identity creation. Each extra voyage through the ladder costs hours of sustained, verifiable attention that cannot be parallelized cheaply.
